Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Got a mail from UAB ahead of time with detailed guidelines as to how to get registered. After filling out all necessary documents and papers, I got my letter of invitation from the host institution.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Very detailed guidelines to do the different steps

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry about not getting the specific course or having to deal with modifications of learning agreement and pre-approval. It will work out in the end.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For MA, I cannot really give a qualified answer, but for BA these courses are first time pre-approved in which this set of courses will now work as a benchmark as to assess future pre-approvals. The courses cover many already known elements but explain them in different ways and through other lenses.

questions.answer: Say yes to everything in the beginning even though it at times might be something you absolute hate because in the beginning it is all about 'networking' trying to find you people

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill vibes

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Keep calm that KU might be extremely slow at times but that it will all work out. Campus is located 45-60 minutes outside the city centre in which commuting is a must. Find yourself good people to work with in all your classes that all courses will include some sort of group work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Embrace the way of life. Don't act all ignorant just because you find certain things weird, it is just different and part of the exchange experience and the overall intercultural learning

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to use my Spanish also in a more academic setting

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: For future mobility preparation, there should be some kind of offer if not compulsory session in which the outgoing students should be prepared better to tackle challenges related to intercultural learning. During my exchange, I have unfortunately encountered many fellow Danish students that did not quite understood the essence of studying and living abroad, resulting in them blaming their lack of understanding on their surroundings among other things that in reality should be a responsibility of their own to understand and solve. I have obviously followed the recent trend of a decreasing percentage of Danish students deciding to not do student mobility in which I really hope that KU will do everything in their powers to turn around that pattern as that and the seemingly 'bad' experiences that I have observed students express will only have negative consequences for the international recognition of KU.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
